meta.notes: Fixed dates recur annually. Year-specific dates use the YYYY-MM-DD format. Sequence offsets are civil days from their anchor, or nominal offsets for lunar fallbacks. Local published calendars supply date overrides.

days.visual_hint: Most sacred night — mosques packed through dawn, tears and supplication at Jama Masjid, Haji Ali Dargah glowing, entire night spent in prayer, believed to be worth a thousand months

days.name: Last Day of Ramadan / Chand Raat
days.visual_hint: Moon sighting for Eid announced, Mohammed Ali Road erupts in celebration, mehndi artists on every corner, last-minute Eid shopping frenzy in Bhendi Bazaar, excitement for tomorrow's Eid

days.name: Ash Wednesday
days.visual_hint: Ash cross on foreheads of faithful at Bandra and Mahim churches, beginning of 40-day fast, solemn services at St. Michael's Church Mahim

days.name: Palm Sunday
days.visual_hint: Palm frond processions at Our Lady of Mount Carmel Bandra, faithful waving palms, church services commemorating Jesus's entry into Jerusalem

days.name: Maundy Thursday
days.visual_hint: Foot-washing ceremonies at Holy Name Cathedral Colaba, Last Supper commemoration, evening mass, altar of repose

days.name: Good Friday
days.visual_hint: Solemn Way of the Cross processions through Bandra streets, churches draped in black and purple, three-hour services, fish markets in Mahim and Bandra busy as meat is avoided

days.name: Easter Sunday
days.visual_hint: Joyous sunrise services, churches bursting with Easter lilies, children's egg hunts in Bandra gardens, festive brunches at five-stars, Afghan Church Colaba packed, resurrection hymns echoing

fridays.note: Every Friday during Lent — fish markets busy in Bandra, Mahim, Sassoon Docks as Christians abstain from meat

days.name: Novena Day 1
days.visual_hint: First novena mass at Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount Bandra, candles lit by devotees, flower offerings to Mother Mary

days.name: Novena Day 2
days.visual_hint: Growing crowds at Mount Mary, wax figure offerings — limbs, houses, babies — placed at the altar seeking blessings

days.name: Novena Day 3
days.visual_hint: Candlelit processions in the evening around the basilica, hymns in Konkani and English, devotees from all faiths

days.name: Novena Day 4
days.visual_hint: Special prayers for the sick, hospital patients sending proxy offerings, healing intentions filling the basilica

days.name: Novena Day 5
days.visual_hint: Thanksgiving masses for answered prayers, grateful families returning with offerings, community spirit building

days.name: Novena Day 6
days.visual_hint: Increasing crowds as weekend approaches, Mount Mary Road beginning to see fair stall setups, anticipation building

days.name: Novena Day 7
days.visual_hint: East Indian Catholic community in full festive mode, Bandra households preparing for the feast, stalls going up along the road

days.name: Novena Day 8
days.visual_hint: Eve-of-feast excitement, Bandra Fair stalls fully erected, street food vendors setting up, entire area transforming into a carnival

days.name: Novena Day 9 (Final)
days.visual_hint: Final novena mass, basilica overflowing, Bandra Fair in full swing — street food stalls for miles, sugarcane juice, pani puri, toys, clothes, massive crowds from all over Mumbai

days.name: Feast of Our Lady of the Mount (Bandra Fair)
days.visual_hint: Mount Mary Feast Day — Basilica packed to capacity, special high mass, Bandra Fair stalls outside the basilica with lakhs of visitors, street food carnival, ferris wheels and games, candles and flowers everywhere, one of Mumbai's most beloved multi-faith gatherings

pitru_paksha.name: Pitru Paksha (Fortnight of Ancestors)
pitru_paksha.note: 16 days — no celebrations, no new beginnings, no auspicious activities. Focus on ancestor remembrance and tarpan rituals.

days.name: Pitru Paksha Begins (Purnima Shraddha)
days.visual_hint: Banganga Tank in Walkeshwar becomes center of tarpan rituals, Brahmins performing pind daan, families offering food to ancestors, somber atmosphere across Hindu households

days.name: Avidhava Navami (Wives' Shraddha)
days.visual_hint: Special prayers for departed married women, families at Banganga Tank, offerings of sindoor and bangles

days.name: Sarva Pitru Amavasya (Universal Ancestor Day)
days.visual_hint: Most important day — tarpan for ALL ancestors regardless of their tithi of death, Banganga Tank in Mumbai packed with families, crows being fed as symbols of ancestors, final grand offerings

navratri_sharad.name: Sharad Navratri (Nine Nights of the Goddess)
navratri_sharad.note: Mumbai civil-day colors for 2027 follow the nine-day sequence published by Drik Panchang.

days.name: Day 1 — Shailaputri
days.visual_hint: Women in turmeric-yellow saris press barley seeds into damp soil beside a copper kalash, a coconut and mango leaves on a low Dadar windowsill.

days.name: Day 2 — Brahmacharini
days.visual_hint: A woman in a leaf-green kurta counts her mala beside a white-robed Brahmacharini print, pausing to straighten the wick of the small brass lamp.

days.name: Day 3 — Chandraghanta
days.visual_hint: Two sisters in grey silk raise a thali of kheer toward Chandraghanta, the crescent above the tiger framed by garlands in a Girgaon pandal.

days.name: Day 4 — Kushmanda
days.visual_hint: A woman in an orange Paithani carries malpua into a Borivali courtyard, her orange pleats picking up the gold reflections from Kushmanda’s lamps.

days.name: Day 5 — Skandamata
days.visual_hint: White cotton sleeves and jasmine braid garlands frame the hands of a Chembur family offering bananas before an image of Skandamata with infant Skanda.

days.name: Day 6 — Katyayani
days.visual_hint: Women in red chaniya cholis pause before garba to offer rose petals at Katyayani’s shrine, their mirrored borders catching flashes from a circling lamp.

days.name: Day 7 — Kalaratri
days.visual_hint: A devotee in royal blue sets a piece of jaggery beside Kalaratri’s lamp, the donkey mount visible in silhouette beyond the brass dish.

days.name: Day 8 — Mahagauri (Maha Ashtami / Durga Ashtami)
days.visual_hint: A woman in a pink sari serves warm puris to girls seated on floor mats, with Mahagauri’s white bull visible on the household altar.

days.name: Day 9 — Siddhidatri (Maha Navami)
days.visual_hint: Women wearing purple gather around a small Navami havan in a Mumbai courtyard, passing a ghee spoon as firelight catches the folds of their saris.

onam.name: Onam (Kerala Harvest Festival in Mumbai)
onam.note: Celebrated by Mumbai's large Malayali community centered in Matunga. Thiruvonam falls on Sep 12, 2027.

days.name: Atham
days.visual_hint: Pookalam (flower rangoli) designs appear at Malayali homes in Matunga, home cleaning, festive preparations begin in South Indian neighborhoods

days.name: Chithira
days.visual_hint: Pookalam patterns grow more elaborate, fresh flowers added daily, Matunga flower shops busy with Malayali customers

days.name: Chodhi
days.visual_hint: Onakkodi (new clothes) shopping, Matunga and Chembur Malayali shops bustling, festive purchases

days.name: Vishakam
days.visual_hint: Onam Sadhya preparations begin, banana leaves purchased, traditional ingredients gathered in Matunga markets

days.name: Anizham
days.visual_hint: Boat race (Vallam Kali) screenings, cultural programs at Malayali associations in Mumbai, Kathakali rehearsals

days.name: Thriketa
days.visual_hint: Visits to Mahalakshmi and Guruvayurappan temples, floral offerings, group prayers among Malayali community

days.name: Moolam
days.visual_hint: Thiruvathirakali dance performances, Pulikali tiger parades at Matunga associations, cultural events

days.name: Pooradam
days.visual_hint: Onathappan clay pyramid statues placed at pookalam centers, anticipation building for the main feast days

days.name: Uthradom (First Onam)
days.visual_hint: First Onam celebrations, early Sadhya feast on banana leaves, Malayali families in kasavu mundu and sari, Matunga alive with Kerala spirit

days.name: Thiruvonam (Main Onam Day)
days.visual_hint: Grand Onam Sadhya — 26-course vegetarian feast on banana leaves, families gathered in Matunga, traditional games, Thumbi Thullal dance, pookalam competitions, King Mahabali's mythic return celebrated, golden kasavu sarees, community joy

days.name: First Sunday of Advent — Hope
days.visual_hint: First purple candle lit on Advent wreaths at Bandra and Colaba churches, Christmas preparations beginning, hymns of anticipation

days.name: Second Sunday of Advent — Peace
days.visual_hint: Two purple candles glowing, peace prayers at Afghan Church Colaba, early Christmas decorations appearing in Bandra's Hill Road shops

days.name: Third Sunday of Advent — Joy (Gaudete Sunday)
days.visual_hint: Rose/pink candle lit alongside two purple ones, Gaudete Sunday joy, carol practice groups in Bandra parishes, Christmas cheer building

days.name: Fourth Sunday of Advent — Love
days.visual_hint: All four candles blazing, final Sunday before Christmas, Bandra churches fully decorated, midnight mass preparations, Hill Road lit up with star lanterns and fairy lights

muktad_parsi.name: Muktad / Fravardigan (Parsi Ancestor Remembrance)
muktad_parsi.note: 10 days before Parsi New Year. Not individually themed but overall ancestor remembrance.

days.name: Muktad Day 1 — Ancestor Remembrance Begins
days.visual_hint: Fresh flowers placed on ancestor prayer tables (ses) at Parsi homes in Dadar Parsi Colony, fire temple prayers begin, sandalwood and frankincense fragrance

days.name: Muktad Mid-Period
days.visual_hint: Daily flower vases refreshed with tuberoses and marigolds, families visiting fire temples — Banaji Atash Behram, Wadiaji Atash Behram — prayers for departed Fravashis

days.name: Muktad Final Day / Pateti
days.visual_hint: Final prayers for departed souls, homes in Dadar Parsi Colony and Godrej Baug cleaned and prepared for new year, transition from remembrance to renewal

days.name: Christmas Eve
days.visual_hint: Midnight mass queues at Mount Mary Basilica and Holy Name Cathedral, Hill Road Bandra glittering with star lanterns, carol singers going house to house, plum cake and wine shopping frenzy

days.name: Christmas Day
days.visual_hint: Bandra's lanes lit with Christmas stars, church bells ringing, families exchanging gifts, East Indian Catholic homes with cribs and trees, Christmas lunch with roast and vindaloo, Colaba restaurants festive

chhath_puja.name: Chhath Puja (Sun Worship Festival)
chhath_puja.note: Huge in Mumbai due to large Bihari/UP migrant community. Major ghats at Juhu, Girgaon Chowpatty, Powai Lake.

days.name: Kharna (Day of Fasting)
days.visual_hint: Devotees beginning 36-hour waterless fast, prasad of kheer and roti prepared, Bihari families in Mumbai preparing for the sun worship

days.name: Sandhya Arghya (Evening Offering to Setting Sun)
days.visual_hint: Juhu Beach and Girgaon Chowpatty transformed — thousands of devotees standing waist-deep in the Arabian Sea offering arghya to the setting sun, diyas floating on water, sugarcane and fruit thekua offerings, colorful saris of women in the golden sunset, one of Mumbai's most visually spectacular festivals

days.name: Usha Arghya (Dawn Offering to Rising Sun)
days.visual_hint: Pre-dawn gathering at Juhu and Chowpatty, devotees offering arghya to the rising sun, breaking the 36-hour fast, emotional completion, sun's first rays illuminating devotees in the sea

durga_puja_bengali.name: Durga Puja (Bengali Community in Mumbai)

2027-10-08.name: Sandhi Puja
2027-10-08.visual_hint: At a Powai pandal, devotees in white and red set a row of oil lamps before Durga as a priest lifts a lotus from a brass tray.

durga_puja_bengali.note: Overlaps with Navratri. Bengali community celebrates at pandals in Powai, Lokhandwala, Shivaji Park.

days.name: Maha Shashti (Durga Puja Begins)
days.visual_hint: Bengali pandals unveiled at Powai and Lokhandwala, elaborate Durga idols with ten arms, dhunuchi dance, dhak drums echoing, community gathering in sarees and kurtas

days.name: Maha Saptami
days.visual_hint: Pushpanjali flower offerings at pandals, nabapatrika (banana plant bride) bathed, Bengali food stalls with luchi-alur dom, cultural performances

days.name: Maha Ashtami
days.visual_hint: Sandhi Puja at the junction of Ashtami and Navami, 108 lamps lit, kumari puja (worship of young girl as goddess), pandal-hopping across Mumbai's Bengali neighborhoods

days.name: Maha Navami
days.visual_hint: Families bring bowls of bhog to a Lokhandwala pandal, where a priest tends the Navami havan and thin smoke catches the light beside the Durga idol

days.name: Vijayadashami — Durga Visarjan
days.visual_hint: Emotional immersion processions from Powai and Lokhandwala pandals, women applying sindoor to the goddess, 'Asche Bochor Abar Hobe' (see you next year), dhak drums playing farewell beats

navaratri_chaitra.name: Chaitra Navratri (Spring Navratri — Gudi Padwa Season)
navaratri_chaitra.visual_hint: At a Girgaon home shrine, a family cups brass lamps before a Durga print and a copper kalash, with fresh mango leaves lit by spring sunlight.
navaratri_chaitra.note: Coincides with Marathi New Year (Gudi Padwa). Very significant in Mumbai/Maharashtra.

days.name: Day 1 — Ghatasthapana / Gudi Padwa
days.visual_hint: Gudi (decorated stick with cloth and pot) raised on every Marathi household's window in Mumbai, Girgaon and Dadar lanes festive, families in traditional Marathi attire, puran poli feasts, neem-jaggery-tamarind eaten for balance

days.name: Rama Navami (Day 9 of Chaitra Navratri)
days.visual_hint: Ram temples across Mumbai celebrating Lord Rama's birthday, special aarti at Wadala Ram Mandir, fasting and feasting, devotional bhajans
